summary: Context meter shows how full an agent's context window is and what fills it. A small pill with a ring and a percentage opens a panel with one bar split by kind (files, tool output, chat, instructions), a legend whose rows list what is in them on hover, and a Compact button that frees room and says how much.
use: When long agent sessions run close to the context limit and people should see it coming.
When people want to know why the context is full, not only how full it is.
When your agent can compact a session, and people should decide when and see what it freed.
When a new tool result can suddenly take a large share and you want to warn about it.
features: `parts` are the kinds of thing in the context, each with a `label`, a `tokens` count, an optional `color` (by default the accent, violet, teal and a neutral grey, in order) and `items`, the list shown on hover. `limit` is the size of the window.
The pill shows the ring and the share used. From `warnAt` of the limit, 85% by default, the ring turns orange.
The bar and the numbers count to their new values whenever `parts` change, so a compaction counts down.
Hovering a legend row lights its share of the bar and shows its `items`.

`message` adds a line under the legend. With `messageTone: 'warn'` it is a warning notice: a faint warning tint, the filled warning sign and the words in the text colour, and Compact takes the warning tint as the action that resolves it. With `'ok'` it is a plain line with the green tick, like "Freed 41.2k tokens. 9 decisions kept". The line takes no room while empty and opens smoothly when a message comes.

Compact calls `onCompact`. Return a promise and, until it settles, the button gives way to a status in its place, a spinner and "Compacting…" with a moving highlight (nothing to press while it runs), while the line beside it says `busyHint` with the same highlight; the row keeps its height. Set `compacted` and the button becomes Undo, which calls `onUndo`.
The pill opens and shuts the panel, and `open`, `defaultOpen` and `onOpenChange` let you control it. The panel folds away when shut and opens back smoothly.

Ships in Clean too (`data-style="clean"`): the pill is a flat secondary control (a hairline and a light fill), the panel is a round card with off-white head and foot strips and its content 16px in from every edge, the bar and its parts keep their colours on round tracks, Compact is a 28px secondary pill 8px from the foot strip's top and bottom and 16px in from the side, on the content's column, and the panel folds away when shut.
a11y: The pill is a button with `aria-expanded` and a label that includes the share used, like "Context, 68% used".
The panel is a region labelled "What fills the context", and it is inert while shut so its controls can't be reached.
Escape shuts the panel while the pointer or the focus is on the meter, and moves the focus back to the pill if it was inside.
The message line is an `aria-live="polite"` region, so a warning or the compaction result is announced.

faq.a: Whatever your agent can tell apart. Files, tool output, chat and instructions work for most agents. Put the largest items of each into `items` so people can see what to drop.

faq.q: How do I show what a compaction freed?
faq.a: Make `onCompact` return a promise, update `parts` with the smaller counts when it resolves, set `compacted`, and pass the difference as `message` with `messageTone: 'ok'`. The numbers count down by themselves.
When the tokens in `parts` add up to `warnAt` of `limit` or more. `warnAt` is 0.85 unless you change it.
